title: ÆTHER: The Architect (global villain theme BGM)
maker: ElevenLabs Music API on the owner's paid plan

request.prompt: A dark, stylish modern film score: the villain's theme BGM of a global big-screen thriller. The villain is a calm, smiling tech billionaire who quietly owns every screen on Earth. Cold elegance and swagger from the first second, growing into crushing power. Cinematic, not DJ music, not EDM, not a club track: it is film music. Full symphony orchestra with menacing low brass and tight strings, a low male choir singing wordless 'ohh' syllables, heavy half-time hybrid cinematic drums, deep sub bass. Written the way today's top South Indian film composers score a stylish villain: a raga melody with slides and fast ornaments, a slick half-time swagger groove, stop-and-slam full-band hits, the hook coming back bigger each time. Raga Simhendramadhyamam in D (like a harmonic minor with a raised fourth): D E F G# A Bb C#. The villain hook, written out: A Bb A G# A, then up C# D, then falls D C# Bb A G# F E D, with gamakam bends on Bb and G#. This ONE hook runs through the whole track, passed between instruments. One steady tempo, 98 BPM half-time feel, never stopping. The villain's own sounds are instruments: a fingertip tap on glass as the click and snap, a deep server-room hum as the drone, soft keyboard clicks as the hi-hat. Real instruments named as themselves are played by real musicians, close, natural and dry, no heavy echo: human whistling, piano, cello section, solo violin, electric cello. Quiet electronic layer underneath: chopped glitching veena stutters and pitched-down mridangam sub hits. 0-4 s: a cold, close human whistle plays the hook alone over a fingertip tap on glass. 4-8 s: a dry low piano and a cello section join under the hook, the server hum drone swells. 8-18 s: full aura: heavy half-time drums with swagger crash in, low brass blasts the hook, low male choir. 18-30 s: the hook on a growling distorted electric cello with slides, fast string ostinato, keyboard-click hi-hats. 30-34 s: drums and bass step out, played by the band, not muted; only the whistle and piano carry the hook, like a thought. 34-46 s: full-band slam: full orchestra and choir, the hook bigger, toms doubling. 46-58 s: a sinister solo violin answers the hook with fast raga runs, a heavy hit on every phrase end. 58-60 s: surprise: everything stops except one fingertip tap on glass, then a full-band slam. 60-78 s: the hook returns one whole step higher in E, full orchestra, choir and drums, the biggest and most powerful moment. 78-90 s: a korvai ending, three heavy rising full-band hits, a final boom, then the whistle plays the first five notes of the hook once more, alone. No soft long intro, no slow or empty middle, no lull longer than 4 seconds, no gaps, no fade-out, no side-chain pumping, no white-noise risers, no build-and-drop EDM structure, no lyrics.

brief.notes: Jithesh 31 Oct 10:01: 'Need 2 global tracks, one is the theme BGM for a villain and one a car chase' (car chase in another thread). Global = worldwide audience, modern concept (30 Oct rule), no country setting. Script first (rule 17). Stylish-villain raga Simhendramadhyamam in D (ragas.md s6). Own written hook and a whistle signature, none of the shared devices (Storm Entry v7 lesson). Hype by 8 s with one instrument first (Dark Horse liked), Zero Hour-style big orchestra. Prompt mode, music_v2, one continuous generation, 2 takes.
